claim: Deployed CBR systems of 1989-1992 (CLAVIER, SMART, Electric Boat valves, GE FormTool) succeeded by retrieving whole past episodes with outcome labels, seeded from expert notebooks or an existing rule base, rather than by modelling the domain.
agent_test: Compare a store of full solved episodes with outcome labels against a rule or summary store at equal tokens on a held-out task set.

claim: Reported deployment gains are builder self-reports without controlled baselines: CLAVIER gives no counts (thousands of dollars per month), Electric Boat about 10 percent / $240K, FormTool $2.4M per year. Only FormTool has a rematch test (cheaper formula for 64 of 100 colours).
agent_test: Do not cite these as effect sizes; require our own matched-baseline run.

claim: SMART lab test: under 50 percent of test cases resolved without the system, 87 percent with it; a later review restates this as over 95 percent of calls, so the figure drifts and N is not given.
agent_test: Treat as unreplicated; re-measure resolution with and without case retrieval on our own queue.

claim: Failed (negative) cases are useful in CLAVIER, and in LLM agents only when distilled into lessons or diagnoses; raw stored failures are noise (ReasoningBank: AWM 44.4 to 42.2 with failures, ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7; Evo-Memory: unfiltered failures degrade baselines).
agent_test: Store failed attempts with labels; measure whether retrieving failures cuts repeat errors versus successes only, at equal tokens.

claim: Validity of a case depends on context (same load valid in one autoclave, invalid in another); retrieval must key on context, not only surface similarity.
agent_test: Tag cases with environment fields; test retrieval with and without a context filter.

claim: Case-based memory lifts LLM agents out of distribution: Memento adds 4.7-9.6 absolute points OOD; CBR ablation raises HLE PM 17.4 to 24.4 and DeepResearcher PM 72.2 (K=0) to 78.5 (K=4).
agent_test: Add a case memory to our agent, ablate it, equal tokens, OOD split.

claim: A small number of retrieved cases is enough: Memento gets most of its gain at K=1 and is flat to K=32; ReasoningBank success falls from k=1 to 4; fallacy work peaks at k=1. The 10 percent of case base is best result is a 4-point grid without variance and is weak.
agent_test: Sweep K at equal tokens and check saturation.

claim: Retrieved cases can hurt: random 1-shot below zero-shot (driving), NOMAD CBR worse than baseline (0.0632 vs 0.0608), larger case bases lowered fallacy F1, retrieved labels matched truth only 27.7 percent.
agent_test: Include a random-case control and a no-case control in any case-memory test.

claim: Raw cases versus distilled insights is task dependent: DS-Agent favours executable past solutions over text insights (rank 2.08 vs 3.41 without CBR); ExpeL insights beat retrieval on HotpotQA (36 vs 31) but not ALFWorld (50 vs 55).
agent_test: Compare raw cases against distilled insights per task type at equal tokens.

claim: Similarity choice matters: ExpeL ALFWorld task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs random cases 42.5 vs ReAct 40.0; CBR-RAG hybrid AnglEBERT k=3 0.9141 vs no-RAG 0.8967 (+1.94 percent).
agent_test: Test retriever variants with a random-case control.

claim: Industrial LLM-CBR deployment evidence exists: Huawei Re4 test-script generation, about 6,000 online samples, +2.75 percent FF1 (DCN) and +10.08 percent (SP) over deployed CBR+SFT; removing the Retain step hurt most (size unverified).
agent_test: Test a Retain step (write solved cases back) against a frozen store.

claim: Naive fine-tuning scored below naive CBR on Huawei units (DCN FF1 49.46 vs 64.01) because outputs need functions beyond model knowledge.
agent_test: Compare in-context case retrieval against parametric update at equal tokens.

claim: The Adapt/revise step carries part of the gain: DS-Agent revise-rank ablation 2.58 vs 2.08, Huawei engineer revision, CLAVIER user edits.
agent_test: Ablate the adapt/revise step with execution feedback at equal tokens.

claim: Persistent case memory gave mixed results over repeated loops (Spaceship Titanic accuracy +0.005 with lower variance; NOMAD worse, p=0.20) with only four seeds.
agent_test: Run more seeds before trusting small case-memory gains.

claim: The primary Mark 1989 CLAVIER paper and Hennessy and Hinkle 1992 were never read; all CLAVIER facts come from Hinkle and Toomey 1994/1995.
agent_test: None.

claim: Unfiltered write-back of an agent's own cases is harmful: add-all memory scored below a small frozen expert-verified memory on four agents (RegAgent 55.48 vs 67.53), and only oracle-checked addition beat the frozen set on all four (70.95). Retain pays when the written case is verified (Huawei Re4 retained human-revised scripts).
agent_test: Gate every write-back on verified success; compare frozen store, add-all and gated add at equal tokens.

claim: On non-agentic reasoning tasks, a curated or distilled memory usually beats plain verbatim retrieval of past pairs and full-history appending (Sonnet AIME 2024 FH 26.7, DR 43.3, DC-Cu 50.0), but the ranking flips by model and task (GPT-4o Game of 24 DR 6 vs BL 10; Evo-Memory ExpRAG beats complex designs).
agent_test: Run raw-case, distilled-lesson and no-memory arms at matched tokens on our reasoning tasks; report per task type.

claim: Case benefit scales with task recurrence and with feedback quality: ReMem gain correlates with within-dataset task similarity (r 0.717 and 0.563); ACE and DC degrade without reliable labels; wrong similar cases are copied (experience-following).
agent_test: Measure task-embedding similarity and judge reliability before adding memory; use a random-case control.

claim: Memento's CBR gain (+3.7 to +6.7 F1, +5.3 to +8.2 PM across three benchmarks) is a same-pipeline contrast, so the offline-online executor contamination (-18.0 F1) does not explain it. A leak through the case bank is not ruled out and no independent replication exists.
agent_test: Replicate with a case bank built only from disjoint training tasks.

claim: No controlled before/after study with N and a baseline was found for any 1990s deployed CBR system, and the primary Mark 1989 and Hennessy and Hinkle 1992 papers remain unread (search tools were rate limited).
agent_test: None; treat 1990s numbers as builder reports.

claim: Distilled reasoning memory can be cheaper than raw memory baselines: ReasoningBank used +4.3% tokens vs +15.1% (Synapse) and +16.8% (AWM) over no memory, while giving the larger gain (+8.3 pts SR on Gemini-2.5-flash vs +1.6 and +3.6).
agent_test: Report tokens per solved task for each memory arm.
